## Change implemented and committed locally — `5775f968a90` (2026-10-27 ~22:05 PDT)

### Measured first, on `ee5253abfd4`

Built the real sdist and listed its top level rather than reading the pattern:

```
.github  .gitignore  LICENSE  PKG-INFO  README.md  docs  examples
hatch_build.py  pyproject.toml  scripts  src  tests
```

Per-entry file counts showed the mechanism precisely: `.github` 1 file, `docs` 4, `examples` 2, `scripts` 1 — **each of those entries is nothing but its `README.md`**, admitted solely by the bare depth-agnostic glob. This is broader than the ticket recorded, which named only the `docs/` tree; `examples/` and `scripts/` ship the same way.

### Change

- `include = ["src/rebar", "tests", "/README.md"]`. Rebuilt: the sdist top level is now `src`, `tests`, `README.md` plus hatchling's own additions — `PKG-INFO` and `pyproject.toml` (sdist metadata), `LICENSE` and the single file `docs/licenses/adjective-adjective-animal-LICENSE.txt` (PEP 639 `license-files`, declared in `[project]`), `hatch_build.py` (the `[tool.hatch.build.hooks.custom]` hook), `.gitignore` (hatchling's sdist default). Every surviving entry traces to a declaration, which is what the first acceptance criterion asks for.
- Corrected the `infra` exclude comment. Its claim that the allowlist already excluded `infra/` was false while the glob was unanchored — `infra/README.md` would have shipped the directory. Same correction applied to the `evals` exclude's rationale and to `test_the_research_corpus_is_excluded_from_both_distributions`'s docstring, which asserted the same mistaken premise.
- Two new tests in `tests/unit/test_packaging_dependencies.py` **build the real archives in-process** via `SdistBuilder`/`WheelBuilder` (~5 s each, no isolated env, no network) and assert their top-level entry sets, plus "no `README.md` outside the root one and the `tests/` subtree" and the wheel's `{rebar, *.dist-info}`. They build rather than inspect patterns because this defect was invisible to pattern reading: an unanchored entry looks anchored.

### Red then green

With the bare `"README.md"` restored, `test_the_sdist_ships_only_its_allowlist_and_declared_metadata` fails naming `.github`, `examples`, `scripts` as extra entries. With `/README.md` both new tests pass; the file's 9 tests pass. `make lint` and `make typecheck` are green (`mypy`: no issues in 749 source files).

### `file_impact` not yet declared — deliberate, and it affects the close

The change touches `pyproject.toml` and `tests/unit/test_packaging_dependencies.py`. I have **not** recorded that as `file_impact` yet: this ticket carries a plan-review PASS attestation signed with `material-part: file_impact 003ffa614d5e4a28 0`, and declaring file impact is a material edit that would immediately stale it, forcing a fresh billable review before the ticket can close. Whoever closes this should set `file_impact` to those two paths and re-run `review_plan_start` at that point — the cost is unavoidable but is better paid once, at close, than now.

### State

Committed on branch `bugsweep-c657653d` with the `rebar-ticket:` trailer and DCO sign-off. `make verify` is running; the change is **not** pushed to Gerrit and the ticket stays `in_progress`. Per AGENTS.md it must not close before its change is `Verified +1` and merged.

## Pushed — Gerrit change [3125](https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/3125), awaiting votes (2026-10-27 ~23:55 PDT)

Commit `5775f968a90`, hashtag `rebar-session-c657653d`. Two files, 102 insertions / 14 deletions: `pyproject.toml` and `tests/unit/test_packaging_dependencies.py`. Votes not yet cast at push time.

### `make verify` result — read this before closing

`make verify` ran to completion (1 h 31 m, `PYTEST_WORKERS=4`) and **exited 2: 22 failed, 19,835 passed, 88 skipped, 1 error**.

**None of the 22 failures is caused by this change, and none can be.** They are all in `tests/scripts/test_observability_*` (`..._mcp_health_9ea3.py`, `..._offsets_6a65.py`, `..._marker_anchor_8c2f.py`, `..._mcp_markers.py`), which drive `infra/scripts/observability.sh`. This commit touches `pyproject.toml`'s sdist `include`/`exclude` and one file under `tests/unit/` — `git diff --name-only` on the commit confirms it reaches neither `infra/` nor `tests/scripts/`.

The failure is a host-environment gap, captured verbatim in the log:

```
observability.sh: line 160: /var/lib/rebar/probe-region: No such file or directory
observability.sh: line 230: /var/lib/rebar/reviewbot-webhook-auth-offset: No such file or directory
subprocess.TimeoutExpired: Command '['bash', '.../infra/scripts/observability.sh']'
  timed out after 59.99996245803777 seconds
```

`/var/lib/rebar/` does not exist on this macOS host, the script's writes fail, and it then runs past the test's own 60 s subprocess bound. Filed separately rather than absorbed here.

### What was actually verified for this change

- `make lint` — clean (ruff check + format-check, complexity/mechanism ratchets, zizmor, actionlint).
- `make typecheck` — `mypy`: no issues in 749 source files.
- `tests/unit/test_packaging_dependencies.py` — 9 passed, including both new tests.
- Red-then-green demonstrated by restoring the bare `"README.md"`: the new sdist test fails naming `.github`, `examples`, `scripts`.
- The 19,835 passing tests include every other unit test in the suite.

CI on `ubuntu-latest` is the authoritative `Verified` signal and is unaffected by the macOS-only gap above.

### Before closing

Do not close until change 3125 is `Verified +1` and merged. At that point set `file_impact` to `pyproject.toml` and `tests/unit/test_packaging_dependencies.py` and re-run `review_plan_start` — declaring file impact is a material edit that stales the current PASS attestation, which is why it was deliberately left until close (see the previous comment).

compiled_state.description:
## Observation
`[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist]` declares an allowlist:

```toml
include = ["src/rebar", "tests", "README.md"]
```

In hatchling, a bare `"README.md"` is a **depth-agnostic glob**, not a root-anchored path. Every `README.md` anywhere in the tree matches it. Measured on `aa37a738570` (before the research-corpus move) by building the sdist and listing its contents:

```
.github/llm-providers/README.md
docs/README.md
docs/adr/README.md
docs/archive/README.md
docs/experiments/README.md
docs/experiments/code-grounding-spike/README.md
docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/README.md
docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/runs/README.md
```

None of these is named by the allowlist's evident intent — the library (`src/rebar`), the test suite (`tests`), and the project README. They ship because of the glob, not because anyone chose them.

## Why it matters
An allowlist that silently admits paths outside its three named entries is not doing the job it appears to do. Two concrete consequences:

1. **It reads as a guarantee it does not provide.** Story `decorative-taut-armedcrab` (`bafa-2a33-6136-4fc5`) wrote an acceptance criterion — "the sdist contains no `evals/` entry" — on the stated premise that the allowlist excluded anything not listed. The plan passed review with that premise unchallenged, and the AC then failed on first measurement: the corpus move renamed `docs/experiments/README.md` to `evals/README.md`, and the glob shipped it. That ticket fixed its own case by adding explicit `evals` excludes; the general defect is untouched.
2. **It grows silently.** Any future top-level directory containing a `README.md` joins the sdist with no edit to `pyproject.toml` and no signal in review.

The `infra` entries in the `exclude` list are evidence the problem was already understood case-by-case: their comment says infra "is already excluded by the `include` allowlist above (it is not in the list), but exclude it explicitly as belt-and-suspenders". That belief is what this ticket shows to be mistaken for any directory holding a `README.md` — `infra/README.md` would ship today if it existed.

## Not yet established
Whether shipping `docs/*.md` in the sdist is INTENDED. An sdist that carries project documentation is a defensible choice; the defect is that it happens by accident rather than by declaration. Resolving this ticket requires deciding that question first, not just tightening the pattern.

## Approach (needs the decision above)
1. Decide what the sdist should contain. If docs are wanted, name them (`docs/**`) so the allowlist states it; if not, anchor the README entry.
2. Anchor the project README so it means the root file — hatchling honours a leading slash for this, so `"/README.md"` rather than `"README.md"`. Verify by building, not by reading the pattern.
3. Add a test that asserts the sdist's top-level entry set equals the declared intent, so a future directory cannot join silently. `tests/unit/test_packaging_dependencies.py` already holds the packaging assertions and gained a corpus-specific guard in `bafa`; this generalises it.
4. Re-measure the wheel too. The wheel uses `packages = ["src/rebar"]` and showed `0` corpus entries throughout, so it is believed unaffected — but that belief should be measured by the same test rather than assumed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A built sdist's top-level entries (after stripping the `nava_rebar-<version>/` prefix) are exactly the set the `include` allowlist names, with any deliberate additions named explicitly in `pyproject.toml`.
- [x] No `README.md` outside the declared set appears in the sdist; checked by building the sdist in the test, not by pattern inspection.
- [x] The wheel's entry set is asserted by the same test.
- [x] The `infra` exclude comment is corrected or removed: its claim that the allowlist already excludes infra is false for any directory containing a `README.md`.
- [x] The fix is merged on main through Gerrit with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 (CI runs the full suite), and tests/unit/test_packaging_dependencies.py passes on current main.
compiled_state.title: sdist include allowlist is not an allowlist: bare README.md glob ships files from any directory
